_comment: THE single source for the credential shapes an MCP server document may never carry. Both languages read THIS file: the web tier generates web/app/lib/mcp/secret-patterns.generated.ts from it (bun run gen:mcp-patterns; check:mcp-patterns fails on drift), and a client-side reader can load it directly. Each regex is plain ECMAScript source, unanchored, matched case-sensitively against the whole raw document text. A shape whose literal is short enough to fall inside an ordinary word carries a (^|[^A-Za-z0-9]) left boundary, so hyphenated prose like task-management-and-scheduling is not read as a key. The entropy block is the belt below the named shapes: a token of at least minLength characters from [A-Za-z0-9_+=-] whose Shannon entropy (bits/char) reaches threshold AND which mixes lower/upper/digit reads as a random secret; a long all-hex run does too. Both rules live in the TS module and are documented there.
_names_comment: The two NAME vocabularies, here for the same reason the shapes are: they decided different things in the two gates until one of them grew a word the other did not have, and a bundle the authority accepted was then refused by every client's update — permanently unplaceable, with no way to tell from either side. credentialHeaderNames are header names that carry a credential by definition, matched case-insensitively and whole. credentialNameWords are read after folding a slot's name to letters and digits, so GITHUB_TOKEN, github-token and githubToken are one word; a slot NAMED for a credential is fine, and the same slot arriving with its value filled in is not.
